description: Healthy simple LED design audited at schematic resolution (no pin connectivity -> no connectivity findings)
why: Healthy simple LED design audited at schematic resolution: parse_schematic cannot resolve pin-level connectivity, so connectivity rules (LED_NO_LIMITER, UNCONNECTED_PIN, FLOATING_NET, NO_DRIVER) are correctly silent; all values and footprints are present -> zero findings expected

description: Same mini-design at netlist resolution: only the passive-only LED_A net advisory
why: Same design at netlist resolution: the only finding is the advisory NO_DRIVER on the passive-only LED_A net (R1+LED1) — no errors, no warnings

description: Fully healthy minimal MCU design at netlist resolution (power rails + driven nets, values and footprints present)
why: Fully healthy MCU design at netlist resolution: every net is either a named power rail (5V/GND) or driven by U1 (BOOT0), every part has value+footprint, no LED, no single-connection nets -> zero findings expected

description: LED design whose R1 has no footprint: not manufacturable (error), rest healthy
why: Simple LED design where R1 has no footprint: MISSING_FOOTPRINT (error) is the contract; the extra NO_DRIVER info advisory on LED_A is an accepted extra (info level, same advisory as the healthy simple-led netlist case)

description: Deliberately broken design: LED straight on the rail, values-less R2, dangling net — all five rules fire
why: Deliberately broken design: LED straight on 5V/GND (no series resistor), a values-less R2 with a single dangling net NC. All five rules must fire with the declared severities and nothing else

description: Partial golden contract focused on the star rule LED_NO_LIMITER; the other findings are accepted extras
why: Partial golden contract focused on the star rule: only LED_NO_LIMITER is pinned; the other four findings of bad-led are accepted extras. Demonstrates the allow_extra_rules semantics on real data
